reasons: The file is a hand-written copy of server types, so drift is likely over time.
Some optional fields are marked optional, but the screens use them without always checking, which can break older runs.

terms.meaning: a written description of what shape a piece of data must have
a field that may be missing from the data
a value that can be one of several named options
the set of slides that make up the exported presentation

sections.name: OutcomeLabel
sections.title: Outcome label names
sections.what: Lists the four labels a project can get: Delivered, Overran, Cautionary, or In progress.
sections.why: Keeps outcome names consistent across screens.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new outcome on the server means changing this list and the color maps in the screens.

sections.name: VerificationStatus, RelevanceStatus, Stance
sections.title: Verification and relevance status names
sections.what: Lists how a fact's source was checked (verified, partial, unverified, unreachable, unsourced), how relevant it is to the project, and the stance a finding takes.
sections.why: Lets the screens color and label each fact consistently.

sections.name: RecipeProject
sections.title: Project shape
sections.what: Describes one project with its location, technology, dates, budget figures, delay, outcome and counts of facts and findings.
sections.why: Holds everything the project comparisons and cases need.
sections.watch_out: Budget values are stored in a unit that is either millions or raw, so a display that forgets the unit can show the wrong size.

sections.name: RecipeFact
sections.title: Fact shape
sections.what: Describes one researched fact with its text, source link, source checks, relevance, pillar and sub-driver routing, and whether it was admitted to the analysis.
sections.why: Holds the evidence the whole result rests on.
sections.watch_out: A fact can exist but not be admitted, so screens must check the admitted flag before counting it.

sections.name: RecipeFinding
sections.title: Finding shape
sections.what: Describes one analyst finding with its text, stance, confidence and the facts it is based on.
sections.why: Lets a finding point back to the facts that support it.

sections.name: RecipeCommentary
sections.title: Commentary shape
sections.what: Describes one perspective from a named person with their role and a paraphrase, plus a link.
sections.why: Shows opinions from named people next to the case they relate to.
sections.watch_out: These are paraphrases, not direct quotes, and the shape does not store a quote.

sections.name: MethodSource
sections.title: Method source shape
sections.what: Describes one source used in the method, with its link, channel type, publisher, year, check date, capture status and the passage taken from it.
sections.why: Lets the method view show how each source was used and whether it was reachable.

sections.name: MethodItem
sections.title: Method item shape
sections.what: Describes one benchmark, framework or practice taken from a method source, with its quote.
sections.why: Holds the claims the framework is built on, each tied to a source.

sections.name: Methodology
sections.title: Methodology shape
sections.what: Describes the whole method section: thesis, searches run, sources, items, rejected item count, provider health and qualifications.
sections.why: Holds everything the Method view and the methodology PDF need.
sections.watch_out: The rejected count is kept only as a number, so the reasons are not available in this shape.

sections.name: SubDriver
sections.title: Sub-driver shape
sections.what: Describes one sub-driver with its letter, text, why it matters, keywords and the method items it rests on.
sections.why: Gives each sub-driver its grounding in the method.

sections.name: Pillar
sections.title: Pillar shape
sections.what: Describes one driver pillar with its name, principle, categories, keywords, grounding, scoring rubric and sub-drivers.
sections.why: Central unit of the framework that the views are organized around.

sections.name: Framework, CellScore
sections.title: Framework and score names
sections.what: Describes the framework as its pillars plus a list of categories that were not assigned to any pillar. Defines the score names used in the heat map.
sections.why: Lets the screens show which categories are not yet covered and color the grid.

sections.name: Assessment
sections.title: Assessment shape
sections.what: Describes how each project scores on each pillar, with pillar-level counts, routing of facts to sub-drivers, and optional routing notes.
sections.why: Holds the scoring behind the heat map and the pillar bars.
sections.watch_out: Several fields are optional, so older runs may not have them and screens must handle that.

sections.name: Discrimination, Cited
sections.title: Discrimination and cited statement shapes
sections.what: Describes how well a pillar separates delivered from troubled projects, with a label such as discriminating or weak. Also defines a statement with the ids of the sources behind it.
sections.why: Tells the user whether a pillar actually predicts outcomes. The cited statement is the basic unit of every claim in the results.
sections.watch_out: The index can be empty, so a missing index must not be shown as zero.

sections.name: SubProfile
sections.title: Sub-driver profile shape
sections.what: Describes the written profile for one sub-driver: its statements, good examples and cautionary tales.
sections.why: Holds the narrative shown in the sub-driver view.

sections.name: PillarProfile
sections.title: Pillar profile shape
sections.what: Describes the written profile for one pillar: its overview, practices, implications and its sub-driver profiles.
sections.why: Holds the narrative shown in the pillar view.

sections.name: CaseSummary
sections.title: Case summary shape
sections.what: Describes a short summary of one project: its headline and takeaways per pillar, each with a direction and sources.
sections.why: Gives each project a readable summary in the synthesis.

sections.name: Synthesis
sections.title: Synthesis shape
sections.what: Describes the overall written conclusions: the executive summary, pillar profiles, case summaries, cross-project comparisons, learning systems, and a count of dropped claims.
sections.why: Holds all the written conclusions in one place.
sections.watch_out: The dropped claim count shows how many statements were removed for lacking sources, so a high number is a sign of weak writing.

sections.name: TraceLine, CaseStance, PillarCited
sections.title: Trace line, case stance and pillar citation shapes
sections.what: Describes one line of progress log with its kind, a case stance name (strength, weakness, mixed or insufficient), and a statement tied to one pillar.
sections.why: Log lines drive the progress view. Case stances drive the case grades.

sections.name: CaseStudy, FailureMode, RecipePractice
sections.title: Case study, failure mode and practice shapes
sections.what: Describes a full case study with its group, performance, outcome, timeline, pillar grades and facts. Also describes failure modes and recipe practices tied to a pillar.
sections.why: Holds the material for the two-page case profiles and the recipes.
sections.watch_out: A case can be marked featured, and only featured cases get the two-page profile. Non-featured cases have less content.

sections.name: PillarLesson
sections.title: Pillar lesson shape
sections.what: Describes the headline lesson for one pillar, with its differentiator, recipe practices and failure modes.
sections.why: Groups the recipe content per pillar.

sections.name: CaseAnalysis
sections.title: Case analysis shape
sections.what: Describes the whole case section: the cases, the pillar lessons, how cases were selected and the count of dropped claims.
sections.why: Holds the selection rule so the user can see how cases were chosen.

sections.name: RecipeV3Result, FactRow, Paged
sections.title: Whole result shape
sections.what: Describes the entire saved result of a run, including scope, projects, facts, findings, method, framework, assessment, synthesis, cases, totals and the deck. Also defines the shapes for fact rows and paging.
sections.why: This is the one object the results screens are given.
sections.watch_out: Cases, the deck flag and some totals are optional or may be absent in older runs, so screens must not assume they exist.

sections.name: DeckSlide
sections.title: Deck slide shapes
sections.what: Describes each kind of slide the deck can contain (cover, summary, agenda, pillar, sub-driver, rubric, heat map, glossary, performance, case summary, learning, method, closing and others), each with its own fields.
sections.why: Lets the slide preview and the exporter read each slide type in a checked way.
sections.watch_out: A new slide kind must be added here and handled in the slide view, or it will not display.

summary: Defines the shape of the Lessons Learnt result data that the screens read, such as projects, facts, sources, pillars, cases and the slide deck.
purpose: Gives the screens a shared, checked description of the result so mistakes in field names are caught while writing code.
why: The top comment says this is a copy of the server's types and must be kept in sync. Reason for copying rather than sharing the types is not stated in the code.
how: The file lists small types first, such as outcome labels and verification statuses, then builds larger shapes from them. The largest is `RecipeV3Result`, which contains every part of a saved run. `DeckSlide` describes each slide type as a separate shape, selected by its kind field.
inputs: No inputs. It is read by the other files in the folder.
outputs: Type definitions only. It produces no data and no visible output.
risks: These types are checked only while writing code. If the server changes and this copy does not, the screens can read missing fields at run time with no warning.
debug: If a field is undefined at run time, compare the saved result with the matching shape here and with the server's version. A slide that fails to show is often a kind value that is missing from `DeckSlide`.
